newsitem.title: DENMARK: DFDS shipping line upped turnover in 1996.
newsitem.headline: DFDS shipping line upped turnover in 1996.

text.p: Danish shipping line DFDS, subsidiary of the J.Lauritzen group, sees 1996 turnover up 12 percent on 1995 at 8.2 billion crowns and maintains expectations of a strong full year result.

DFDS turnover in 1995 was 7.3 billion crowns, with 18 percent from passenger line activity, 16 percent from freight, 14 percent from onland transport and the rest from logistics and forwarding operations, DFDS managing director Niels Bach told a financial analysts' seminar on Sunday evening.
Bach declined to go into more detail about DFDS' 1996 result but reiterated previous optimism about achieving a "very satisfactory" whole year result.
DFDS, with seven passenger ferries and 17 roll-on roll-off vessels, last August posted interim profits of 61 million crowns, compared to a first-half 1995 loss of 25 million crowns.
The unit's pre-tax profits fell to 82.1 million crowns for whole year 1995 from the previous year's 271 million crown surplus.
Operating profits for 1996 are forecast to be within the 150-180 million crown range, compared to 110 million crowns in the previous year.
Looking ahead, Bach said the expected ending of duty free shopping within European Union member states in 1999 might force the shipping line to close one of its routes.

"The end of EU duty free shopping will hit us but only in a limited way. To adjust to the coming situation DFDS has sold one ship already, leased out another and will have to close a route, possibly the Gothenburg (Sweden)-England route," he said.
The J. Lauritzen group is expected to announce its full year 1996 result, including that of the DFDS unit, at end-March.
DFDS' Scandinavian Seaways plies between Scandinavia and Germany to England, operating ferry services also to the North Atlantic Faroe Islands and a daily Copenhagen-Oslo route.
